A central feature of aging is inflammaging, a state of chronic low-grade inflammation driven by cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and oxidative stress. Recently, two regulated forms of non-apoptotic cell death-ferroptosis and cuproptosis-have emerged as critical mechanisms linking redox imbalance, mitochondrial stress, and disrupted metal homeostasis to age-related pathology. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent process characterized by lipid peroxidation and impaired glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) activity, and cuproptosis, a copper-dependent mechanism associated with protein lipoylation stress, both intersect with aging-related changes in mitochondrial and metabolic function.
